# frontend specification

> Status: design settled (**v2 = Console v2 + capture store**). Fully reorganized from v1 (feature tabs) into **role tabs**, and then every screen was moved off runs/episodes onto **captures**. The Japanese version is canonical (treat it as the source of truth). The English version `docs/specs/en/frontend.md` is an auto-generated mirror (do not edit it directly). **No authentication is required.**

A backend-driven, lightweight Web UI (Vite + React + TypeScript). Tabs are organized not by technical function (v1: Live / Graph / Probe / Recordings / Validation / Datasets / Config) but by **"whose job is it"** — 6 tabs: **Collect / Review / Datasets / Validation / Monitor / Settings**.

## Roles

| Tab | Whose job | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Collect | Operator | Run recordings, judge immediately, improve |
| Review | ML engineer | Judge recording quality and labels, feed them into datasets |
| Datasets | ML engineer | Compose logical datasets, catalog them, (future) build them |
| Validation | Robot engineer | Run pipelines, standardize validation |
| Monitor | Robot engineer | Diagnose communication, signals, the system and **store health** |
| Settings | Robot engineer | Robot configuration, plans, and their scope of effect |

Core concept: **recording quality and task result are separate axes** (a failed task ≠ bad data; failure data is kept, labeled, and used for training). Recording proceeds in a **Batch > Episode** hierarchy persisted by the orchestrator ([api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Batch"; the Session level is **TBD**: Phase 2.5).

**What v2 (capture store) changes across every screen**:

- **Every screen reads the `captures` API.** Not one call to `/api/v1/runs` or `/api/v1/episodes` remains. v1's feature tabs (`RunsTab` / `DatasetTab` / `inspect`) and the in-browser bridge `episodeBridge` have been **deleted**.
- **testids are keyed by `capture_id`** (by `membership_id` for dataset members). Never by row number or by position within a batch — two batches holding the same number would collide.
- **The Availability chip** (below) states, in one vocabulary across every screen, whether a recording's bytes are on this machine right now.
- **Deletion is two separate dialogs, Discard and Delete** (below).
- Monitor gained a **Store health panel** (rebuild / corrupt / SUSPECT / Repair).

## Implementation

- Base: **Vite + React + TypeScript**.
- State: **Zustand** (UI state) + **TanStack Query** (server state; SSE events are folded into the cache). Routing is URL-query based (`?tab=<id>`).
- Charts: unified on **uPlot** (axis ticks, crosshair, series overlay, zoom). UI: **Tailwind CSS** (components are hand-rolled).
- Live video: **WebRTC** (connects to `webrtc_streamer`'s `/stream/offer`).
- Tests: **Vitest + Testing Library**.

## Inputs

- WebRTC video (`webrtc_streamer`; by default same-origin via `/webrtc`, reverse-proxied by the frontend's nginx; override with `WEBRTC_PUBLIC_URL`)
- Numeric-field sample streams (`topic_probe`; same-origin via `/probe`; used by Monitor's Signals view)
- REST / SSE (`api_orchestrator` `/api/v1`)

## Tabs and navigation

- **The 6 tabs are fixed in the frontend** (`V2_TABS`). v1's "driven by the backend `tabs` registry" mechanism is **retired** — the `tabs` field of `GET /api/v1/config` remains for compatibility, but v2 does not use it for display or ordering.
- **All legacy tab ids redirect** to preserve deep links: `live`→`collect`, `graph`/`probe`→`monitor`, `runs`→`review`, `dataset`→`datasets`, `config`→`settings`.
- Every tab is URL-addressable (`?tab=<id>`). **`?tab=<id>&solo=1` renders only that tab, with no tab bar** (the ↗ button on each tab opens it in a separate window — the multi-window way to line up several charts). Solo gives the URL tab priority as its initial display; Collect begins batch restoration after hydration of the saved operator is complete. Moving from Collect to another tab preserves `solo=1`.
- **Header (shared by all tabs)**: the 6 tabs, a **ROS_DOMAIN_ID badge**, a **connection chip** (the SSE connection state), and an **OP chip** — click it to set the operator name (persisted in localStorage; sent as `operator` on every subsequent `/record/start`). Solo Collect has an OP chip too.

## Parts shared by every screen (v2)

### The Availability chip

Derived from `capture.replica.state` and `capture.digest_state` by a **single decision function**, and drawn as the same chip by Review / Datasets / Validation. "Is it usable" (`usable`) is a value derived from this chip, and it is the shared precondition for running jobs, previewing, and archiving.

| replica.state | Display | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `null` (no row) | not here yet | No copy on this machine yet. **Normal in the split deployment** (you pull from the robot after review). Not an error |
| `present_verified` | verified | Here, and the digest has been confirmed to match |
| `present_unverified` + `digest_state=pending` | verifying | Here, but verification is still running |
| `present_unverified` | here | Here |
| `trashed` | in trash | In `.trash` (awaiting the reaper) |
| `absent_managed` | removed | kairos deleted it deliberately |
| `missing_unmanaged` | missing | **It disappeared outside of kairos.** A warning |
| `corrupt` | corrupt | The sidecar cannot be read. A warning |
| an unknown value | unknown | A state this console does not know. **Surfaced as a warning** (the server may be newer = treat the whereabouts of the bytes as unconfirmed) |

The point is to **never blur `verifying` into `verified`**. Show something as "verified" before it has been verified, and the display stops meaning anything at all.

### The two deletion dialogs (Discard / Delete)

**They are deliberately not one shared component.** Fold two things whose wording, required fields and weight of confirmation differ into a single part, and a change to one leaks into the other.

| | Discard (not uploaded) | Delete |
|---|---|---|
| Purpose | Discarding data that was never uploaded | Ordinary deletion |
| reason | **Mandatory** (an empty field disables the confirm button) | Optional |
| Wording | States plainly that it cannot be undone and there is no restore | "The files go away, but the catalog keeps the record, so we can still answer where they went" |
| Count · size | Always shows the number of items and the byte total (`(size unknown)` if not known) | Same |

- The reason the reason is mandatory is stated right there: "it goes into the lifecycle ledger; once the files are gone, that one line is the only record of why they were deleted".
- **In the split deployment both dialogs carry the caveat that a copy stays on the robot** (split is detected from `available` in `GET /api/v1/transfer/status`). The discard side says it honestly: "this deployment records on a separate robot. What is discarded is **the copy on this recording PC**; a copy may remain on the robot, and kairos does not delete it."
- Bulk runs are sequential, show progress (`{done}/{n}`), and **report failures honestly, per capture**. Cancel is blocked while a bulk run is in flight.
- `409 capture_busy` comes back naming the lease holders and their expiry. The dialog lists **every holding job from `details.holders`** (count, job_id, expiry), adds `lease_expires_at` as "resolves on its own by this time if you do nothing", and offers **"Cancel those jobs and retry"** — a state where waiting is the only option is not left standing (the lease refuses the delete, so the delete side must be able to reach the lease). The button cancels each job sequentially (a refused cancel is named in that job's own words; the rest continue) and **auto-retries the delete exactly once**. **A second 409 updates the display to the fresh holders and stops** (no loop — every lap destroys someone's work). The button states plainly that cancelling stops running validation/preview generation — that work is lost. Non-job holders (transfer, digest) are noted as not cancellable from here.

## Screens

### Collect — run recordings and judge immediately

- **Context bar**: Robot (real selection; the same robot catalog as Settings) / Project · Task · Condition (pickers fed by Plans, plus Custom free input) / **Batch number** / episode progress "n / target".
  - **The Plans catalog (Projects → Tasks → Conditions) is server-synced**: each level has a canonical `project_id` / `task_id` / `condition_id` and a display name. Collect freezes both the IDs and labels of a selected Plan in Batch / Start context; Custom and unmatched labels use `null` IDs rather than guessing a nearby choice. Legacy name/string localStorage is normalized to deterministic IDs and persisted. Sync uses GET `revision` and mandatory PUT `base_revision` CAS; on a 409 conflict the local draft remains and is not retried automatically. Settings offers an explicit **Use server catalog** action as the only server-adopt recovery. Responses are checked against a send generation, so an old success cannot clear a newer dirty edit.
  - The batch number is the **server-issued `batch_seq`** (per robot × local date, restarting from 1 each morning). Before a batch exists, show a **prediction** — "next #N · assigned on first recording" (today's max seq + 1) — which settles to the server value on the first recording. There is no "planned batch count" denominator (it has no real referent).
- **Batch / Episode progress is server-persisted**: Start waits for Batch allocation (creating it with `POST /api/v1/batches` when needed) before sending `collection_context`. An empty batch has no row and consumes no number. After operator hydration completes, reloads / tab switches restore only batches filtered by **all of** `status=active`, the active robot, and the operator (the number prediction alone reads at robot scope). If several match, it never selects the newest by itself and shows a persistent notice that restoration was not performed.
- **Batch menu** semantics (End early / Reset **never delete recordings**):
  - Pause / Resume (currently local only; server-side is **TBD**: Phase 2.5) / End batch early (`status=ended_early` + reason) / Reset (a **complete no-op** for an empty batch; with recordings it closes the current batch and the next recording starts a new number) / Change condition (PATCH) / **Change target (2026-07-14)**: set the batch's planned `target_episodes` (1–500, PATCH; inherited by the next batch; lowering it below the recorded count is flagged up front as completing the batch immediately). **The strip's chip count, "n / target" and the completion check all follow the target** (the UI's fixed 30 is gone — a value the API always had and the UI ignored). End / Reset do not move to a local terminal/reset state, success display, or modal close until both recorder-stop confirmation and the Batch PATCH have server confirmation. On failure, they retain the batch and show Retry. Target changes, starting the next batch, and completion from reaching the target likewise show success and commit locally only after their corresponding server confirmations. **Report issue is not displayed until there is a route that can persist its receipt.**
- **Recording controls**: Start / Stop. A Batch API failure does not block Start: recording may proceed with `batch_id=null` and the current context labels, while the UI states the reason and retry path without claiming Batch progress. **Pre-arm (two-phase start, 2026-07-14)**: on a robot with `recording.pre_arm` (default on), while the tab is visible and the phase is ready/result the screen keeps the recorder armed via `POST /record/prepare` (a keep-alive re-prepare just before `disarm_at`; best-effort — failures are never surfaced, Start simply falls back to the conventional full synchronous path). Prepare context is provisional; the actual Start metadata is what the manifest adopts. While armed, a "pre-armed · instant start" chip sits next to the Start button and the SYSTEM STATUS Recorder row shows `ARMED` (both **read the server-reported state** — never lit merely because a prepare was sent). The Required data row also gets real measurements before recording, from the armed session's subscription snapshot. Arming gate (waits for subscriptions to be established; an "N matched · N missing" note), failed-start banner (**plain wording leads, the raw code follows** — `already_recording` and the rest are mapped into operator language), **recorder cache/drop detection banner** (`dropped_messages` + a cache-setting hint, gated to that capture). **Browser recording sounds (2026-08-19)**: operators opt in per device from the Collect speaker control (default off), which provides volume and Start / End / Warning previews. Sounds play only in the tab that initiated the operation; reload, takeover, and the initial status read are silent. Start plays only when the recorder confirms that the `capture_id` started by that tab is both `state=recording` and present in `live_capture_ids`. End plays only after a normal Stop has been confirmed terminal and absent from the live set (it does not mean that data quality passed). Warning plays once for a failed Start, an unconfirmed Stop, an unreachable recorder during recording, or an unexpected end; the existing persistent visual state and `role=alert` remain authoritative for the reason and recovery. Start / Stop presses, arming, flush, quick check, and reload are silent, and an audio playback failure never changes recording state. **Keyboard**: `R`=Start / `S`·`Space`=Stop / `Esc`=Cancel arming / `?`=shortcut list (disabled while an input field is focused; button labels carry a hint such as `· R`). On each phase transition, focus moves to the next primary action (never falls to the body).
- **External operator actions (2026-08-23)**: three vendor-independent logical actions LEFT / CENTER / RIGHT for hands-busy operation (teleoperation and the like) — tied to no foot-pedal product, driver, or SDK: programming the same chords onto any generic HID macro device is sufficient, and development and testing are complete on an ordinary keyboard. The bindings are `Ctrl+Alt+1/2/3` (read from the physical `code` — layout-independent; no bare printable key, no browser default, no collision with R / S / Space / Esc / `?`). The meaning of each slot is **derived by one pure function from the current machine state, and both the shortcut handler and the always-visible HUD (`ExternalActionHud`) consume that same resolution**, so the display can never drift from the behavior. State table: READY = CENTER Start; RECORDING = CENTER Stop; SAVING / QUICK CHECK / ARMING / PAUSED / ENDED / COMPLETED and takeover = everything disabled; RESULT (before Failure) = LEFT selects Failure, RIGHT = Success + Save; RESULT (Failure selected) = LEFT / CENTER / RIGHT = the current Task's configured reasons + Save (an unassigned slot gives **visible feedback only**, never saves, and there is no silent fallback to `Other`). Failure-reason shortcuts are accepted **only after Failure has been explicitly selected** (stamping a reason during READY / RECORDING is structurally impossible). Input guards: typing (input / textarea / select / contenteditable), an open registered modal / overlay, saving / quick check in flight, takeover, auto-repeat (`event.repeat`), and keydown latching (one physical press = at most one logical action; keyup releases the slot on the **physical key alone**, so the slot cannot stay latched even when the modifiers are released before the digit). `Success + Save` and `reason + Save` are **single compound steps through the machine** (`saveSuccess` / `saveFailureWithReason` — reading the live store snapshot instead of a render closure, the same save flow the mouse Save uses; `saveFailureWithReason` is a no-op unless Failure is already selected in the result state), not sequential pick+confirm React updates. The existing R / S / Space / Esc / `?` and mouse controls are unchanged (fully usable as a fallback). The HUD always shows the three slot labels plus their current meaning (disabled reads "—", unassigned reads "Unassigned"), and in Failure mode it also names the current Task.
  - **Keyboard-only acceptance scenario (no mouse)**: configure failure shortcuts for one task in Settings → Plans (assign a reason from the shared failure-reason vocabulary to each of the LEFT / CENTER / RIGHT slots) → in Collect with the same task selected, Start with **CENTER** (`Ctrl+Alt+2`) → Stop with **CENTER** → Success + Save with **RIGHT** (`Ctrl+Alt+3`) → next take: Start with **CENTER** / Stop with **CENTER** → select Failure with **LEFT** (`Ctrl+Alt+1`) → reason + Save on any assigned **LEFT / CENTER / RIGHT** slot → verify in Review that **both episodes** landed correctly (first = Success, second = Failure + the chosen reason).
- **Recording state is server-truth** (5s polling of `GET /record/status`; HCD fix 2026-07-14): if a recording this browser did not start, or has lost sight of, is running, a **RECORDING IN PROGRESS card** (run_id / elapsed / size / operator / topics, a `Stop & save` behind a confirm modal, `Open in Monitor →`) appears instead of READY. The Recorder row of SYSTEM STATUS comes from the same query = the "READY yet 409" contradiction cannot arise structurally. Regular Stop, takeover Stop, and End / Reset on an already-active batch treat a recording as stopped only after not just the `200` from `POST /record/stop`, but `confirmRecorderStopped` confirms a terminal state and absence from `live_capture_ids`. A late start cancelled by End while arming waits for cancelled-start reconciliation to complete: verifying status ownership so another driver is not stopped → stopping completes → discarding beyond the digest lease (it does not falsely fail by waiting for a global terminal state after another driver has started recording). A take recovered by stopping shows up under "Unsaved-take recovery" below. Record-topic resolution matches v1 (selected / configured / all; the selection is shared with Monitor's Rec column, and the "REC N topics" chip jumps to Monitor; Start is disabled on an empty selection).
- **Saving an episode**: Stop → a real-event gate (resolve the stop API → **confirm the recorder stopped** → read integrity; the fixed timer is retired, and a failed stop stays in SAVING with `Retry stop`) → the result panel. **A `200` from stop is not enough to move forward on (2026-07-27)**: `POST /record/stop` is idempotent and, when it cannot find anything active, answers `200` with the most recent run — so **a recording that is still going looks like a success**. After it resolves, `GET /record/status` is therefore **polled — one immediate check, then every 1 s** — and the screen only moves forward once the stop is confirmed (a terminal state AND absent from `live_capture_ids`) (revised 2026-08-07). **A transient status-read failure is not a failed stop** (2026-08 addendum, timing sweep S2-2): the recorder's status route takes the same lock as its finalise, so a 503/timeout lands exactly while a large bag flushes. The confirmation loop swallows read failures and keeps polling until the deadline — only the deadline may surface an error. **The same confirmation loop is shared with Settings' robot switch (stop & switch)**, closing the path that hot-swapped the config mid-flush (timing sweep S2-5). The flush (rosbag2 draining its cache) takes seconds and is **normal progress**, not an error, so while waiting the SAVING card shows an elapsed "flushing (Xs)" counter, and only past the recorder's escalation budget (SIGINT 30s → SIGTERM 30s → SIGKILL 5s plus margin ≈ **70 s**) does it route into the existing `STOP_FAILED` path (`stop_not_confirmed`, `Retry stop`) and stay in SAVING. Without that, the screen advances to labelling a take that is still being written, and the only thing left to end it is the `MAX_RECORD_SECONDS` auto-stop. **Success is the default selection**, so a clean success is a single `Save — success` action (Enter works). Failure branches from ✕ with a mandatory reason (the reason choices are the shared vocabulary edited in Settings > Failure reasons; 2026-08-04 — the fixed array is retired). **The automatic quality prefers the server's settled `quick_check.verdict`**, falling back to the real integrity only while it is still unsettled (clean → `Good · auto`; drop/failed → `Needs review · auto` plus the real drop count — nothing is made up). It can be overridden freely from `change` with the three choices (good / needs_review / not_usable). **Saving is `PATCH /api/v1/captures/{id}/review`** (a CAS that requires `base_revision`). The payload sends `quality` + `quality_source='operator'` only on an override; with no override it omits `quality`/`quality_source` and lets the server derive them (the capture's settled `quick_check.verdict` is the single source of the automatic quality; even when the save lands before settlement the server corrects it afterwards — [api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Late re-derivation after settlement"). The operator's steps and keystrokes are unchanged (the omission is a payload-side change only). **Only once the server has settled, a receipt** `Saved — Episode n of Batch m · {operator}` (a transient ring on the strip chip). Discard is a **real delete** that goes through the Discard dialog (**reason mandatory**; "The two deletion dialogs" above) — `POST /api/v1/captures/{id}/delete {kind:"discard"}`. **Retake (2026-08-05)**: one button on the result panel — "discard THIS take (ledger reason = superseded by retake) → immediately start the next recording under the same labels" — folding the dozens-a-day discard → re-pick → restart into one action. A failed discard never auto-restarts. **The Storage row prefers the recorder's OWN disk** (`disk_free_bytes` on `GET /record/status`; the robot's disk in the split deploy) and, while recording, adds "≈N h left" from the live write rate (no estimate in the first 10 s or while idle — nothing is made up).
- **Unsaved-take recovery**: even if you leave between Stop and Save, on reload an amber banner "Unsaved take from {time} — {N} MB, {duration}" (`Label it` / `Discard` / `Later`) lets you recover it (it detects the most recent capture that is in a terminal state and has `review_revision == 0`). Label saves to the original Batch only when a non-null `collection_context.batch_id` can restore that Batch's detail. If it cannot be fetched, recovery does not proceed by guessing another Batch. Older recovered takes with `batch_id=null` remain ungrouped and are never connected by inference.
- The "n / target" count is the **monotone counter `episodes_recorded`** (what was recorded is the truth; a deletion in Review never decreases it; if it diverges from the quality breakdown, a footnote says so).
- **COVERAGE side card**: sends the current Plan IDs (name fallback when unresolved), active robot, and hydrated operator as its complete scope. Until that scope is known it shows why it is waiting rather than mixing totals across robots or operators. Rows are the plan conditions ∪ conditions actually observed in that scope (the `condition_id` / name pair). The Σ `episodes_recorded` advances on the first review save and never falls on exclude / delete; the card states its scope so **"what to record next" is decided from data**.
  - **The "exported" column was dropped in v2.** Under §6 a dataset became a named set of captures and has no condition of its own, so the old count **has no source left to derive it from**. Better to show no number at all than a number nobody can derive.
- **The episode strip places each chip on its true episode number (`index_in_batch`)**: drawing by array position lets a deletion in Review pack the later chips leftward, producing the off-by-one where the newest episode reads as "not recorded". A recorded number with nothing surviving behind it is distinguished honestly by a dashed chip plus "recorded earlier; no longer listed (deleted in Review)". When the server re-allocated the `index_in_batch` of a save (a cross-terminal collision), the response value is adopted for the local chip too. **The server restore merges only within the same batch** (so a just-saved chip does not flip back to not recorded). A restore onto a different batch never carries the local count over.
- **Cameras**: WebRTC previews. Panes can be added/removed (**manual adds capped at 4**; the initial panes the stream config defines are not bound by that cap — a robot config deliberately lines up 5+ cameras in real use, and sub panes are forced to low resolution, so the subscription-budget principle holds). The main pane has resolution presets; sub panes are force-capped to low resolution (240/360p). **Latency / fps live in an overlay chip at the top-right inside the preview video** (per-tile measured values, threshold colors; never placed outside the video). Pre-connect placeholders state the reason for their state (an empty tile must not read as a failure).
- **Active warnings card (extended 2026-07-15, revised 2026-07-27)**: the union of two real-data signals — ① the arming snapshot's uncaptured targets (current values while `armed`, frozen at start-time while recording) + ② **firing monitor alerts** (the SSE `alert` buffer; hz/gap threshold breaches = **mid-recording degradation**, surfaced on the screen the operator is looking at). ① **never merges the causes**: only `missing_topics` (no publisher) is asserted as "N target topics not publishing", while `unsubscribed_topics` (published, recorder not subscribed yet) gets its own "not subscribed yet" wording — displaying a topic that Monitor shows at 30 Hz as "not publishing" is a lie, and it sends the operator off to fix the wrong thing (with both present it asserts neither: "not being captured" + the breakdown). Alerts are **restricted to the recorded topics** (the arming matched∪missing∪unsubscribed set when present, else the config `default_topics` patterns, else everything — broader beats silently hidden). Rows carry the measured value (`joint_states Hz < 45 · now 38.2`), cap at 2 + "+N more in Monitor", with an "Open in Monitor →" path. Shown while idle too (so you notice "the robot is off today" before you start recording). The System status card gains a **Topic rates row** (`N / M at expected` — of the topics the monitor judged, how many are status=ok; `unknown` stays out of the denominator, and "—" when the monitor is down). No composite score is built (it would hide the causes).
- **Quick check** (the post-stop quality summary): the result panel shows the `quick_check.verdict` the server settled at stop time (good / needs_review + human-readable `reasons`), polled gently from the capture detail `GET /api/v1/captures/{id}` (~3 tries / 5s, stopping once settled). While unsettled it shows only a subtle "Quick check running…" note (nothing is made up), and **saving never waits on settlement**. The evaluation is designed as a two-layer "settlement of the monitoring statistics accumulated during recording" — Layer 0 = the statistics the monitor / recorder hold during recording (counts, drops, gaps, expected_hz ratio; final at stop), Layer 1 = read only the MCAP summary section (O(index)). It must hold **in ≤5 s with zero transfer, even in the split deployment** (details in [api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Stop-time quick check").
- **Advice** is a single fixed mock (hold still ~1s), visibly titled `General tip · static guidance` so it cannot be mistaken for episode-specific analysis. **Generation logic is TBD (Phase 3)**. Only the approach is settled: live advice takes the orchestrator's aggregated SSE metrics as input; deep advice takes the transferred MCAP (dora never touches DDS).
- Fits **without scrolling** from 3840×2160 down to 1366×768 (compact density toggle). Collect is an operational console rather than a reading column, so on desktop it uses the available width and height while preserving the left control column + right camera column arrangement and the video aspect ratio. Fixed `max-width` / `max-height` values must not leave most of a large display empty.

### Review — judge quality and labels, feed datasets

The stored `loss_report` keeps its per-topic aggregates and additionally shows above-threshold gaps as a **list of time band, topic, gap length, and estimated missing count** (not a heatmap). It states that the estimate comes from median cadence and does not establish the missing position or cause. It runs only when the user presses "Run loss report", never automatically after recording ends.

- List + detail of completed recordings. Each row is one capture (`GET /api/v1/captures`) and shows **Batch "MM/DD · #N" / Task result / Quality / lane / the Availability chip**. Filterable by operator and so on. **The list follows the cursor all the way to the end** (it does not silently cut off at 200), and the header carries real-data tally chips (`n ready · n needs check · n excluded` / `n success · n failure`). The displayed number is the **persistent `index_in_batch`** (a deletion never renumbers it). The decision buttons are a **fixed bar outside the scroll**.
- **Exception-review model**: a capture whose quality is good (or operator-confirmed) is **READY** with no extra click. Only **NEEDS CHECK** (quality not good and still unjudged) forms the work queue, resolved with "Mark OK — include" or Exclude. The default order is NEEDS CHECK → READY → EXCLUDED.
- **Condition context**: Review/Datasets use immutable `collection_context.condition` as the collection-time authority for display and search (an explicit `null` means "not recorded" and never falls back to the current Batch). Only legacy captures without context fall back to the current value from `batch_id`; loading and failure are stated as unavailable. Review Inspection shows this read-only **directly below Task**.
- **Review saves are a genuine CAS** (`PATCH /api/v1/captures/{id}/review`; [api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Saving a review"). **Nothing is optimistically committed** — the optimistic edit is displayed, but it is rolled back if the save fails.
  - **`409` (conflict)**: a banner stating "someone else saved first. Reload and re-apply your edit — the two edits are not merged", and it **names the value currently stored on the server** (`It is now {review_status} · {quality}`). To do that it re-fetches `GET /api/v1/captures/{id}` best-effort.
  - **`500` (the sidecar write failed)**: a red banner that **must be dismissed explicitly**: "**Not saved.** …nothing was saved — `record.json` could not be written. Fix the free space or the permissions, then save again". It must never disappear on its own like a toast (if it does, you walk away believing a save happened when it did not).
- **Datasets is the entry point for feeding a dataset** (one function, one place). Review carries the judgement, and once READY is reached it offers the path to Datasets. v1's **move** via "Export ready (n)…" is gone — a dataset became a logical set, and the recorded bytes do not move ([capture_store](capture_store.md) §6).
- **Deletion is two-step**: Exclude = "Excluded — kept on disk" (non-destructive, label only) → only the excluded items get the Delete / Discard path ("The two deletion dialogs" above; bulk runs sequentially and reports failures honestly). **The single-row Exclude has no confirmation dialog** — it takes effect immediately, from the row and from the detail panel alike (not a byte of the recording goes, and it is one action to put back; the dialogs are kept for the two things that cannot be taken back, Delete and Discard). Instead, right after an Exclude an **Undo band** (`role="status"`) appears directly under the list toolbar and **puts back the `review_status` / `quality` / `quality_source` that the Exclude overwrote, in a single save**. That memory is client-side, session-scoped and covers **only the most recent one** (the server has no "previous review" to ask for, and an Undo button is not a reason to grow the schema). `quality` is sent explicitly even when it is `null` — omitting it means "no change", which is how `not_usable` would survive — but **the server re-derives an explicitly-null quality from the quick check**, so a quality no operator had ever set goes back to being machine-judged (the toast says so). **The offer disappears the moment the capture is no longer excluded** — by Return, by Adopt, or by another terminal's save arriving on a sweep. An offer that does not disappear will, taken later, silently overwrite the newer decision with the older value. From EXCLUDED and from confirmed exceptions, "↩ Return to review" puts the item back to pending (reversible). But **pending is not a finished state**, so returning one states the remaining step: "Adopt to include in datasets".
- **Detail inspection**: manifest / validation / loss_report table / on-demand mp4 "Video check" player / each JSON block. `fast_validation` can also be run from the detail. **"All cameras" submits every camera topic of the capture at once** (§7.1 is a shared reader lease now, so read-only jobs no longer exclude each other on one capture; actual concurrency is throttled by `KAIROS_DORA_MAX_CONCURRENCY` — the side that owns the work — and the client never queues). The old one-at-a-time serialization, with its "Queued behind n…" note, existed only to dodge lease contention and is removed along with the note.
- **Data integrity section (the former Signals section, redesigned 2026-07-15)**: runs `signal_report` behind an explicit button and shows, in order, **① the synced video (video_check's full-length mp4) → ② the aggregated integrity timeline directly beneath it → ③ a ranked loss-event table → ④ a per-topic summary (message count · continuity · loss-event count)**. The timeline is **one lane** (the worst condition across all topics overlaid: green = nothing wrong / amber = minor / red = major, or silence on a dense topic / gray = no topic active); hovering names the degraded topics, clicking seeks the video (only when the full-length video is loaded — with a head-only preview it would be a lie, so it is disabled). **Empty bin = red is restricted to dense topics (median non-zero density ≥ 3)** — measured on real data, the bin width (~10 ms) fell below the message period (20–30 ms) and painted healthy data solid red. Loss on sparse topics is carried by the backend's loss_events (1.5× the median interval). The event table ranks **majors first, then by duration descending**, shows the first 8, and folds the rest behind an explicit "Show all n events" (the count is always visible = nothing is hidden silently). **The former raw waveform chart (the per-field uPlot plot) and the field-picker UI were removed** (a raw joint-angle waveform does not answer "is this episode usable"; live waveforms are Monitor > Signals = topic_probe). The Settings signals-defaults editor and `GET/PUT /api/v1/config/signals` were removed along with it.
- **Batch filter + batch-level bulk decisions**: clicking a row's batch chip narrows the list to that batch (click again / ✕ / Clear to leave). While filtered, the header offers "Exclude batch (n)…" (**the confirm modal is kept for the bulk action only** — it moves n captures at once. What it saves is the same as the single-row Exclude: Not usable + excluded, **the recordings stay on disk**, sequential saves, per-row failures reported honestly — but **it carries no Undo band**. The way back is "↺ Return batch", and running the bulk exclude clears the single-capture Undo offer, which would otherwise read as the undo for what was just done) and "↺ Return batch (n)" (bulk-restores the excluded ones to pending). One action to keep a batch that FAILed batch-level validation (Validation) out of the mix. Section-grouping of the list (full grouping) is **deliberately not adopted** — it would break the exception-review work order (NEEDS CHECK first).
- **Importing external bags (2026-08-05)**: Review's **"↧ Import bags…"** brings in rosbags recorded outside kairos, a FOLDER at a time. Enter the folder as the server sees it and **Scan** (`GET /api/v1/imports/scan`) lists the bag directories **one level inside it** (that depth is a decision; name the subfolder for a deeper tree, and a folder that is not a bag is simply not listed rather than reported as a failure — but when it HOLDS bags one level down it is offered as a hint, "<name> (N)", that drills in on one click, so an empty result is never a dead end) — each with its topics / messages / duration / size, or **why it cannot come in** (no `metadata.yaml`, with the `ros2 bag reindex` remedy; already imported; no `.mcap`). Seeing all of that **before anything is copied** is the point. Importable rows are pre-selected; pick **Copy (default) or Move** and the run imports them one by one, **skipping a failed bag with its reason on the row and carrying on** (stopping at the first bad directory would leave the operator hand-importing the rest). One bag becomes one capture under `objects/<capture_id>/` (staged in `.incoming/`, atomic-renamed into place), named `imported_YYYYmmdd_HHMMSS`. **Before running, a bulk label (operator / task / robot) can be entered** — each optional, applied to **every bag of that run** and stamped into the captures' birth manifests (not §4.3 review overrides). A field left empty is **not sent** (an empty string would be a label that exists yet says nothing). `operator` offers the plans roster as a datalist while staying free-text. An invalid label (contains `/`, or over 255 **bytes**) is refused in place **before any request is sent**, keeping the inputs (the server would answer the same with a 400 and import nothing, but that is indistinguishable from a per-bag 400 such as a missing `.mcap`, so the two documented conditions stop client-side). Left empty, bags come in unlabeled as before — label them per capture in Review. After that it is an ordinary capture: validate it, put it in a dataset, archive it. The copy is asynchronous, so the list is refetched a few times after a run.
- **Validation verdict badge and override (2026-08-05)**: the detail panel shows `VALIDATION PASSED` / `VALIDATION FAILED` / `NOT VALIDATED` — the server's derived verdict, rendered as-is, so the screen can never disagree with what the dataset gate will do. `NOT VALIDATED` says plainly that nothing has checked this recording; it is not a pass. A FAILED capture cannot join a dataset, and a **reason-required override** (kept in the ledger) lets it through or withdraws that permission. Collect surfaces a `needs_review` verdict one line after Save — discovering it days later in Review means a re-setup, not a retake.
- **Label editing (operator / task / robot)**: the detail panel's Inspection rows are **editable in place** (click the value → three inputs → Save labels). The main use is the **imported bag** — the recorder only stamps these on recordings it started, so a directory that came from outside is born unlabeled and stays invisible to the operator/task filters. **Unset shows "Set operator…", not "—"**, to signal it can be filled. The three go in **one request**, on the **same CAS path** as the existing review (`base_revision`; 409/500 handling identical). Whitespace-only is sent as `null` to **clear** (= back to the recording's own manifest value). A refusal keeps the in-progress inputs, states the reason in the operation's own words, and **never claims a save happened**.
- **Failure reasons are visible**: the `failure_reason` picked at save time is shown as the tooltip of the list's FAILURE chip and, in red, under the detail panel's Task result field.
- **Transfer in the split deployment**: split is detected from `available` in `GET /api/v1/transfer/status`, and when it applies, alongside the Availability chip's `not here yet` a "transfer to the recording PC" action appears (`POST /api/v1/transfer/pull {capture_id}`). **Completion is not announced by the transfer API** — what the frontend watches is the capture's **replica state**, which turns `present_unverified` the moment the reconciler adopts the arrived directory. v1's `bag_local` boolean was retired (it could only say "here / not here", and **could not tell a copy that never arrived from a copy that was deliberately removed**). Transfer is **manual pull only** (no automatic scheduler is being built), and **transfer and validation are separate buttons** (never auto-chained). Auto-pull on the first review save is opt-in via `transfer.auto_pull_on_save`.

### Datasets — composing logical datasets, and the catalog

**In v2 a dataset became a logical set** ([capture_store](capture_store.md) §6). The recorded bytes never move out of `objects/<capture_id>`; a dataset is nothing but a DB row plus ledger events. This tab is therefore not "the catalog of what has been exported" but "**the place where sets are composed**".

- **Composition**: add to a dataset from the candidate rail (captures that reached READY in Review) with `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/members`, and remove with `DELETE …/members/{membership_id}`. **Not one byte moves**, so taking something out and putting it back, or putting one capture into several datasets, is free. A `display_index` gap never goes to a different recording, but **re-adding the same capture returns it to its original number**. The candidate rail **leads with what can be added**: rows that cannot be (not adopted / bytes elsewhere) are folded by default, expanded via "Show blocked (n)" with the count stated (expanded rows keep their per-row reasons). Candidate rows, member rows, and the selected-member detail show the **collection-time Condition** alongside Task / Operator / Task result. Only legacy captures without a snapshot use Batch fallback; unavailable is never shown as an empty value.
- **Candidate predicate and Bulk Add provenance**: each confirmed Bulk Add run appends its frozen `selection_query` (states / review statuses / present-on-instance / date range / dataset exclusion / `AND` / `OR` predicates) and matched/attempted/succeeded/failed counts to `POST /api/v1/datasets/{id}/selection-recipes`. Summary shows this complete server search as history. Manual add and Combine never fabricate a recipe. If saving fails, successful members are not rolled back; the UI states "members added but recipe not saved" and keeps the dialog open.
- **Candidate predicates and bulk add**: the former single free-text input is replaced by **explicit predicates** combining a field (`Any field / Operator / Task / Condition / Run ID / Capture ID / Task result`), comparison (`contains / equals`), and value. Added predicates remain visible as removable chips, and the whole set is joined with either `AND` or `OR` (a comma is ordinary text, not syntax). Candidates are shown one server-search cursor page at a time; Next / Previous retain boundaries only for display, without accumulating the whole catalog in the browser. Changing the dataset or predicates returns to the first page. **Bulk Add does not operate on the displayed page**: it passes the full matching set frozen by `POST /capture-selections` to a server-owned bulk run. The confirmation dialog also displays this frozen count, so paging cannot change the execution target.
- **The list shows one shelf at a time**: an Active (the default = active + archiving) vs Archived toggle (in the URL as `dsview`). Sealed records never mix into the working list. **The whole-catalog scope is removed** — in a list that mixes per-dataset numbering, #N identifies nothing — so with nothing selected the center shows a placeholder inviting a selection (the old "All datasets" row is gone).
- **Label editing**: the header's "Edit" (rendered only while active) → a three-field modal for name / operator / task (`PATCH /datasets/{id}`). The dialog states explicitly that the members and their numbers do not change. A dataset recorded by several people may leave operator empty (every recording keeps its own operator).
- **Combine**: the left column's "⧉ Combine" → a name for the new dataset plus the sources (a checklist of active datasets, pick order = numbering order) → run. **The sources are never written to** (a dataset is a list, and reading a list does not change it). The implementation is nothing but the ordinary create + add-member in bulk, under the standing bulk rule (sequential, `{done}/{n}` progress, per-capture failures listed honestly, Cancel blocked while running). A capture present in two sources joins once, at its first appearance. Archiving the new combined dataset later runs into the shared-member `409`, so the sources must be cleared up first (deleted, or the members removed) — deleting a dataset touches no recording.
- **URL state is held as `dataset_id` / `membership_id`** (`url.ts` owns only the `ds*` keys and never touches `tab` / `solo`). **Names are editable and `display_index` is for display**, so these two are the only stable ids. A URL that specifies `dsmem` with no `dsid` is dropped.
- **Label filters + manifest**: task-result chips (All / Success / Failure) + an operator select + a search box narrow the list. "Manifest (n)" downloads the filtered result as a JSON manifest (`data_dir`-relative paths + every label) — **materializing the training-set definition as one version-controllable file**. When everything is hidden it says so explicitly: "n hidden by the filter".
- Every member row and candidate row carries the **Availability chip** (above). **A capture that is not usable (missing / trashed / not here yet) is never a target for a job, a preview, or an archive.**
- Detail = DatasetDetail (metadata / member list / topics / loss report / mp4 Video check / sidecar JSON). Jobs run against `capture_id` (`params.dataset_dir` is retired).
- **Per-capture archive**: the button appears only when the candidate meets all three conditions — "an archive root is configured", "it is a member of no dataset", and "its availability is usable". The dialog shows **both** the destination and `<destination>/<capture_id>`, and the confirm label is "Copy, verify, then remove".
  - The success toast is `Archived to {dest} — verified, then removed from this machine`. **A completed response is itself the verification claim** (per-file hashes are compared as the copy lands, and a mismatch fails the run before the source is deleted), so there is no "copied but unverified" response branch (2026-08-11, sweep S4 — the always-True `verified` flag and the unreachable warning branch that read it were removed). A verification failure surfaces as the run's failure.
- **Per-dataset archive (§6.1, the terminal transition)**: the header's "Archive dataset" appears **only when it can succeed** (a root is configured, the status is active, and there is at least one member). The dialog gives the same boundary presentation as the per-capture one (a root picker plus a **Path input** — a freely editable path prefilled with the views shape `<operator>/<task>/<name>`; it echoes the final `<root>/<path>` and states that a path already in use is refused with a 409), plus a **mode radio**: "Copy out — keep them" (seal only; confirm label "Copy, verify, then seal") and "Move out — remove them" (deletes the sources; "Copy, verify, then remove"). When members are shared with another active dataset, **Copy is the default and the dialog says why (n shared)** — a Move the server would refuse with a 409 enumerating them. The archived banner also keeps the modes honestly apart (Copied to … stays on this machine / Archived to … removed from this machine). After the `202`, **the same dialog turns into a progress view**, polling `GET /datasets/{id}/archive` at 1-second intervals and drawing `{done} / {total}`, the capture being copied, and the halt reason. **A halt is generally not a failure to be dismissed**: the run stays `archiving`, and Resume (a re-POST with no destination) picks up from where it stopped. The one exception is a halted attempt for which the server returns `cancelable=true` (zero completed members): the dialog shows "Cancel archive run" and states before the action that the dataset returns to Active, the destination claim is released, and destination files are not deleted. It is not shown for a partially completed run. `cancel_blocker=archive_canceled` is presented as an abnormal state where cancellation is durable but the catalog update is pending, and neither Cancel nor Resume is shown. The completion toast is `Archived to {dir} — n recordings verified, then removed from this machine`.
  - **The status is a badge, part of the row's identity** (archiving = amber, archived = gray, on both the list row and the header). archived is read-only: a banner names the destination and when, and the members' Remove / Discard / Delete and the BuildRail's add controls are **not rendered** (the server refuses them all with `409`, so putting them up would be putting up buttons guaranteed to fail). The dataset's Delete is disabled with "Kept: this record is what remembers where the dataset went." — **the archived row is the queryable cache of the migration log** and is never deletable.
- **Delete** ("The two deletion dialogs" above). Deleting the dataset itself is `DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}`, and it **never touches the captures' bytes** (archiving / archived are `409`, as above).
- **Build** (conversion to LeRobot v3 and the like) and **Recipe-style dataset construction are unimplemented (TBD: Phase 2)** — the UI shows muted shells only, never dressed up as working controls.

### Validation — pipeline execution, standardized

Keeps v1's functionality as-is; only the layout is v2.

- **Pipeline-agnostic**: pick a pipeline (every enabled one from `GET /api/v1/pipelines`) → **pick the targets**: captures (v2 has lost the "before / after export" distinction, so there is neither grouping nor a `dataset_dir` branch; only captures whose availability is usable can be targeted) → **the parameter form** (auto-generated from `schemas.pipeline_forms[<id>]`; an `x-suggest`-annotated string becomes a picker over the target capture's real topics, with the first one auto-seeded — video_check's `topic` needs no hand-typed camera path) → create a durable Validation Run (with a required `request_id` and either one-off `capture_ids` or a server selection's `selection_id`). The target picker shows Next / Previous one server-search cursor page at a time and clears page-bound selections on navigation. All / Batch freezes a server selection rather than using the displayed page. Results are drawn by a **generic renderer** that renders `summary.json` shape-independently (PASS/FAIL badge, message, a key-value tree of metrics, artifacts, raw JSON). **An artifact whose path is data-relative (normalised by the orchestrator) is rendered as fetchable via `GET /api/v1/files/{path}`**: images (png/jpg/svg/gif/webp) render **inline**, anything else becomes a download link, and an absolute path that cannot be normalised stays plain text (never fabricate a link that would 404). So **a plugin that writes a plot image into its report dir gets a graph in the UI with no UI changes**. **Adding a plugin requires no edits to this tab** ([dora_plugins.md §2.5](dora_plugins.md)).
- Only the bundled `fast_validation` has a dedicated checklist against the template's required-topic list. Results can be downloaded as CSV.
- **Bulk execution**: "All completed captures" freezes the server search for terminal captures available on this installation with `POST /api/v1/capture-selections`, then creates one durable Run from its `selection_id`. The browser does not issue one `/jobs` request per capture; it displays the Run detail's per-capture state and PASS / FAIL result.
- **Per-batch bulk validation** (the blast-radius decision = bulk validation only, no alert persistence): picking from the target selector's "Batches" group snapshots a server search containing the `batch_id`, rather than the displayed page, and creates one durable Run for every capture whose availability is usable. It is not disabled merely because the current page shows no candidate. This is the one-click entry point for verifying defects that cluster per batch, such as calibration drift.
- **One-click validation presets**: preset buttons from `GET /api/v1/validation/presets` (`pipeline` + fixed `params`). Bulk-run against **not-yet-validated captures** (`pending_capture_ids`). Shows "N pending"; at zero it is disabled as "up to date". Defined in the per-robot config `config/<robot>/validation_presets.yaml` ([config.md](config.md)).
- **Cancelling a running Run**: a **Cancel run** control under progress sends a durable intent to `POST /api/v1/validation/runs/{run_id}/cancel`. It remains `cancel_requested` immediately after the request and does not pretend completion until the server confirms that child work stopped. Canceled children are shown as **CANCELED**, distinct from failure, and a refusal remains until dismissed.
- **A Run outlives the browser**: the Run's source of truth is the server's `validation_runs.db`; the URL's `vrun=<run_id>` restores the same progress after tab navigation, reload, another window, or an orchestrator restart. Before receiving the create response, the browser saves the same required `request_id` and complete payload in sessionStorage so a reload resends the same intent rather than creating another Run after response loss. A missing or unavailable Run URL is shown as such, never as idle or success.
- Because the backend has no lifecycle or promotion contract, do not show fabricated Experimental / Candidate / Standard chips, Promote, or New run controls. Show only enabled pipeline facts and “Lifecycle and promotion are not configured in this console.”

### Monitor — communication, signal and system diagnostics

The merge target for v1's Graph / Probe / Live health panels. The sub-nav is **Overview / Topics / Signals / System / Store / Events / Logs**. Every sub-view is built on real data (unobtainable values show "—"; an empty chart or empty list states why). The default view is Overview.

- **Context strip**: REC · run_id · elapsed while recording, STANDBY otherwise (a real display, from `record_status`).
- **Overview view** (the diagnostic landing, default): the record context, a topic-health tally (`ok`/`warning`/`danger`/`inactive` counts + the topics needing attention by name → click to chart them in Topics), a summary of firing incidents (the real alert buffer), a compact `GET /api/v1/system` snapshot, and jumps to Topics/Signals.
- **Topics view**:
  - **Add / remove chart panels (max 4)**. Per panel, pick a metric (**Frequency / Bandwidth / Max gap / Rate vs expected**) and the topic overlay (max 6). The time window (30s / 1m / 5m) and **Freeze charts / Live** (formerly Pause) are global — the freeze is charts-only (it says so: `Charts frozen · table still live.`; the table deliberately stays live). Since the window accumulates from when it was opened, while the accumulation is shorter than the window it honestly shows `{window} window (n so far)`. Chart height **follows the measured slot** (the root fix for the bug where a fixed height was clipped by an overflow-hidden parent and the low value range became invisible). **The recording's REC / STOP markers** overlay every panel. Frequency carries the expected_hz reference line. **Latency / loss are not on the menu** — a non-intrusive monitor cannot measure them (per-run loss is provided by Review's post-hoc analysis).
  - **Topics table**: every discovered topic + live metrics (Hz / bandwidth / gap, status dot `inactive`/`danger`/`warning`/`ok`/`unknown`, a shortfall badge with a reason tooltip on threshold breach; shortfall is observed, not true loss). **The Rec checkbox column** = the topic selection for the next recording (not a mid-recording change). Configured topics are pre-checked. Switching robots reseeds from the config defaults. Independent of the chart series selection.
- **Signals view** (v1 Probe, ported): a generic plotter that overlays the **numeric fields** from `topic_probe` per (topic, field). Pick a topic → a numeric field (arrays expand to `[0..N]`), and **overlay several fields across different topics**. Sample-rate selection (1/5/10/30 Hz, default 10 Hz), window, Pause. **Decoding is carried by the isolated `topic_probe` container and never spills into recording or monitoring** ([topic_probe.md](topic_probe.md)).
- **System view** (full page): host measurements (CPU% / GPU% / disk usage · `GET /api/v1/system`; unobtainable values show "—") + ROS_DOMAIN_ID / service endpoints (`GET /api/v1/config`) + **component health**. Health is expressed only from signals the browser can honestly observe: orchestrator = the live SSE pipe being open, monitor = the `bridge` event. `bridge=null` (not reported) is not treated as connected; it displays **checking**. It states explicitly that per-container recorder / streamer readiness is judged by the orchestrator's **server-side `/readyz`** (for the Docker healthcheck) and is not exposed at the browser origin (`/readyz` is not proxied on the same origin, so it is not fetched). A compact **System card** is embedded in the Overview / Topics right rail.
- **Store view (new in v2)**: polls `GET /api/v1/store/health` every 30 seconds to surface **the states that never appear in the capture list** ([api_orchestrator.md](api_orchestrator.md) "Store health and SUSPECT").
  - **The SUSPECT block**: "Suspect — automatic clean-up is halted" + the reason + the time it latched. It **spells out both what is halted and what is not** (halted: the automatic missing transition, the reaper, digests / not halted: recording, saving reviews, browsing). It states that it does not re-fire on every pass, and that only a repair clears it.
  - **The Repair button** is enabled only under SUSPECT. `409 volume_unidentified` is displayed with its reason and disables the button. On success both the store-health and the captures caches are invalidated.
  - **The corrupt list**: path, reason and capture id, plus **which scan it came from** (`corrupt_source` of `reconcile` reads as "reconciler pass", otherwise "rebuild") and the time it was observed. An empty display **distinguishes** the two cases: "no scan has run to completion in this process yet — this is not an all-clear" and "the last {rebuild|reconciler pass} could read every sidecar it found".
  - **Whether deletion is available** (`delete_available` / `delete_unavailable_reason`): when `objects/` and `.trash/` are on different filesystems, it explains on the spot why the deletion APIs return `503`.
  - **The rebuild summary** (`rebuilt_at` + the breakdown) and the **warnings**, plus the most recent reconcile result.
  - The global Store Health banner on every main / solo screen can Dismiss **only informational notices** explicitly classified by the API in `dismissible_warnings` from a successfully completed rebuild that has a `rebuilt_at`. The browser keeps the acknowledgement in localStorage using the `instance_id`, `rebuilt_at`, and warning text as its identity, so the same notice stays hidden across navigation and reloads while a later rebuild or different warning appears again. Dismiss does not change server health, batches, captures, counters, or the rebuild report, and the details remain in Monitor > Store. The same action cannot hide `SUSPECT`, currently corrupt sidecars, unavailable deletion, an unavailable health response, or a rebuild warning absent from `dismissible_warnings`. If localStorage cannot be read or written, the notice remains visible.
  - If reading the health itself fails, it says "**the store's state could not be read, so nothing below is known — this is not an all-clear**". Blankness is never dressed up as "nothing wrong".
- **Events**: SSE `alert`s **collapsed to one row per incident (topic × metric)** — while firing, `firing · since {t}` updates the current value in place; on clearing it flips to `cleared · {t}` (muted); a re-fire shows `×n`. The **Events card** in the Overview / Topics right rail shows the collapsed rows; the **Events view** (full page) adds a topic substring + state (firing/cleared/all) filter and a note (history is session-local, since Monitor was opened). Topics with no config rule are picked up too, by the monitor's default DANGER incident (persisting ~10s) = **the table's DANGER and Events do not contradict each other** ([topic_monitor.md](topic_monitor.md)).
- **Logs view**: a session-local timeline of the SSE lifecycle events received (record_status / alert / job) with type chips + a text filter (a ring buffer capped at ~500). Honestly labelled "since this page opened / the full logs live in `docker compose logs`". Metrics are not recorded (high-frequency noise).

### Settings — robot configuration and plans

The active robot has a manual **Setup check** (`POST /api/v1/system/setup-check`). It never runs on screen load or after recording; only a button press performs the read-only recorder-precondition, ROS topic-coverage, monitor receive/resolved-QoS, and camera-preview checks, keeping next actions visible per blocker/warning. It also states that "the monitor received at least one sample" is not proof that the payload is valid.

- **Robots**: the robot list (committed `config/<robot>/` and gitignored `config/local/<robot>/`) and selection (`POST /api/v1/config/select` hot-swaps recording / stream; recorder QoS / monitor expected_hz apply after a restart — the UI says so. **Activating while recording shows a "Stop and switch?" confirm modal**). **A non-active robot's config is viewable read-only** (`GET /api/v1/config/robots/{robot}`; a "Read-only — {robot} is not the active robot." banner + disabled JSON that can be read as a template). **Aspect** (recording / stream / validation / validators) option selection. The recording config is edited and persisted as JSON (`PUT /api/v1/config/recording`. **Inline validation**: invalid JSON disables Save with a plain error; saving while recording shows an "applies from the next recording" info banner). The stream config is edited and persisted with the same kind of JSON editor (`GET/PUT /api/v1/config/stream`; **`panes` applies immediately to Collect's camera panes**, and the saved note honestly states that `columns` is unused by the current layout. A robot without a config dir gets an explanation instead of an editor. **A file that exists but fails to load is disclosed with a "broken — saving replaces it" amber warning** — never silently presented as a clean empty `{}`. A server-side change while editing is disclosed in an amber banner with the unsaved edits kept). Creating a new robot is not possible — `+ Add robot` opens not a disappearing toast but a **persistent explainer that shows the next step** (create a `config/<robot>/` folder + use an existing robot as a template). The bottom of the rail retires the sourceless version display in favour of the **active robot's real values**.
- **Projects & tasks (Plans)**: edit the Project / Task / Condition definitions. A **shared store** with Collect's pickers reflects them immediately, and they are **persisted server-side** (`PUT /api/v1/plans`. 2026-07-14 — one label vocabulary shared across every terminal. Offline, localStorage stands and dirty edits are re-pushed later. **Modelling** Plans (ids/references/target counts) remains Phase 2.5). Reject blank trimmed names and case-insensitive duplicates in the same scope before PUT, with no success receipt. Task / Condition deletion confirms what disappears from Collect and that saved recording labels remain, with a Cancel path.
- **Failure shortcuts (per Task, 2026-08-23)**: each Task can assign one reason from the SHARED Failure reasons vocabulary to each of the LEFT / CENTER / RIGHT slots (the fast paths Collect's external operator actions save after Failure is selected; the vocabulary itself is not reduced to three). A slot may stay unassigned, and **the same reason cannot sit in two slots of the same Task** (the UI disables a reason another slot of the task uses, and the server refuses it with a 422 as well). A catalog without `failure_shortcuts` (pre-feature) loads as fully unassigned — no migration, normalized on read.
- **Operators** (2026-08-05): the attribution roster (**not authentication** — no passwords, no permissions). Once names exist, the header OP chip **turns from free text into a picker** and keeps the full name visibly present (initials or a tooltip alone are insufficient). While the roster is non-empty **recording cannot start until a name is picked** (kills unknown_operator and spelling variants). Empty the list to fall back to free text with no gate. Blank and case-insensitive duplicate names are refused, and deletion requires an impact confirmation. Shared across terminals via `operators` on `PUT /api/v1/plans`.
- **Failure reasons** (2026-08-04): add / rename / remove the "What failed?" chip vocabulary Collect offers on a Failure. Same shared store / server persistence as Plans (the `failure_reasons` field of `PUT /api/v1/plans`), so every terminal offers the same choices. Blank and case-insensitive duplicate values are refused before PUT; deletion confirms that only future choices change and existing labels remain. **The last remaining reason cannot be removed** (a Failure label requires a reason, so an empty vocabulary would soft-lock the flow). Edits shape **future labels only** — already-labeled episodes keep their stored strings. **Referenced task shortcuts must never go stale**: renaming a reason **carries the referencing slots to the new name**, and removing one **unassigns its slots and says so** — both in the SAME combined catalog edit (vocabulary + plans in one PUT), so an intermediate catalog the server would reject is never persisted.
- **Recording**: the active robot's recording config shown **form-first** (`GET /api/v1/config/recording`: compression / start gate [`start_paused`] / cache [`max_cache_size_mb`] and the default_topics table [expected Hz, QoS-override badge]). The raw JSON editor is demoted to "Advanced" (collapsed by default, `PUT /api/v1/config/recording`).
- **Data quality**: from the aspect content of `GET /api/v1/config/robots/{robot}` — the expected-Hz reference rates + the monitor's warn/danger thresholds (`monitor.warn_shortfall`/`danger_shortfall`) + the active validation template's required topics (a read-only card). Beneath it, the **alert-rules editor** (`GET/PUT /api/v1/config/alerts` → `config/<robot>/monitoring/alerts.yaml`. It applies on monitor restart = stated in the UI). **The form and the Advanced raw YAML are two editing surfaces of the same file, so they guard each other** (2026-08-04 bug fix: while the raw side has unsaved edits the form Save is disabled with the reason inline [it used to silently write the form state, destroying the raw edits — while the screen kept showing the never-sent YAML as if saved]. Save YAML states that it discards the table's unsaved edits. A successful save **force-re-seeds both views from the server response** — a response identical to the cache never fires the effect). The former signals-defaults editor was removed at the same time as the Review waveform chart (2026-07-15).
- **Validation**: the validation / validators aspect selection (`POST /api/v1/config/select`) + the one-click preset list (`GET /api/v1/validation/presets`, pending counts). Execution links to the Validation tab (one function, one place).
- **System** (read-only): deployment facts (ROS_DOMAIN_ID, endpoints, data dir/storage, component health). The version row is omitted because the client has no honest version source. RMW/DDS is not exposed by the API, so only a note is shown.
- **Honest placeholders**: **Dataset profiles** (awaiting the Phase 3 recipe model) and **Users & permissions** (nothing to manage in the single-LAN, no-auth scope) are placeholders that state their reason and nothing more (no dead controls).

## Data flow (SSE × cache)

- Subscribe to the single SSE stream (`GET /api/v1/events`) and fold each event type into the TanStack Query cache. Components subscribe to keys and re-render.
- SSE disconnection is surfaced in the UI (the header connection chip) with automatic reconnection (`Last-Event-ID`).
- **Freshness discipline** (2026-08-11, sweep S3-5/S3-6): (a) a `record_status` SSE event is **not applied to the cache while the status poll is failing** (`setQueryData` clears the query's error and stamps `dataUpdatedAt: now` — resurrecting an unreachable recorder as "fresh"; a replayed post-reconnect event can be minutes old. The event is still logged). (b) Monitor's Topics table **withholds measured columns** while SSE is not open or the monitor bridge is down (never render a frozen snapshot as current; same gate as Collect's system card, with a note saying why).
- **The job-watcher idiom** (sweep S3-4): "on terminal, fetch the result and setState" is **never written inside a queryFn** — with two tabs sharing the cache, only the observer that fetched last runs its setState, leaving the rest with an eternal spinner over a succeeded job. The status queryFn stays pure; terminal handling is an effect on the observed state (shared hook `useJobCompletion`).

## Outputs (APIs called)

- Recording: `POST /api/v1/record/prepare` / `start` / `stop`, `GET /api/v1/record/status`
- Batch: `POST /api/v1/batches`, `PATCH /api/v1/batches/{id}`, `GET /api/v1/batches?status=active`, `GET /api/v1/batches/{id}`
- **Capture**: `GET /api/v1/captures` (filters, cursor), `GET /api/v1/captures/{id}`, `PATCH /api/v1/captures/{id}/review`, `POST /api/v1/captures/{id}/delete`, `GET /api/v1/captures/{id}/archive/config`, `POST /api/v1/captures/{id}/archive`
- **Datasets (logical)**: `GET/POST /api/v1/datasets`, `GET/DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}`, `POST /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/members`, `DELETE /api/v1/datasets/{dataset_id}/members/{membership_id}`
- **Store**: `GET /api/v1/store/health`, `POST /api/v1/store/repair`
- Transfer / retention: `GET /api/v1/transfer/status`, `POST /api/v1/transfer/pull`, `GET /api/v1/retention`
- Topics / system: `GET /api/v1/topics`, `GET /api/v1/topics/status`, `GET /api/v1/events` (SSE), `GET /api/v1/system`, `POST /api/v1/system/setup-check`
- Config: `GET /api/v1/config`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/config/recording`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/config/stream`, `GET /api/v1/config/options`, `POST /api/v1/config/select`, `GET /api/v1/config/robots/{robot}`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/config/alerts`, `GET/PUT /api/v1/plans`
- Files: `GET /api/v1/files/{path}` (video_check mp4 · job artifact images/files)
- Jobs: `GET /api/v1/pipelines`, `POST /api/v1/jobs` (`{ capture_id, pipeline, params }`), `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/status`, `GET /api/v1/jobs/{id}/result`, `GET/POST /api/v1/validation/templates`, `GET /api/v1/validation/presets`
- **No longer called**: the `/api/v1/runs` family, the `/api/v1/episodes` family, `/api/v1/datasets/{op}/{task}/{index}`, `/api/v1/datasets/export(-all)` (all retired; there are no compatibility aliases)
- Probes (the only two direct connections that do not go through the orchestrator): `/probe` (topics / fields / SSE sample streams), `/webrtc` (offer / ICE)

## Design principles

- **Honesty principle**: never display what cannot be measured (no faked latency / loss; shortfall ≠ loss). Never fabricate a value — a value that cannot be obtained and an evaluation that is not implemented show "—" or an explicit mock label. Never conflate quality with task result. **Never make "could not be read" look like "nothing wrong"** (Store health's empty display, Availability's unknown).
- **Explain a failure in the words of the action that failed.** An error message states not "what happened" but "what became of the thing you just did" (`Not saved.` / a `capture_busy` that names the lease holder). The failure of a destructive operation never becomes a disappearing toast. (The split-discard toast wording is "a copy may remain on the robot" — true both for a confirmed split and while the probe is unanswered.)
- **A deadline at the fetch layer** (2026-08-11, sweep S3-8): every request gets a default 30-second deadline (`AbortSignal.timeout`), so a half-open TCP connection cannot become "an eternal spinner on whichever screen made the call". Calls whose server-side budget is longer override it — `record/stop` 90s (never cut the recorder's ~75s escalation off client-side), `record/start` / `prepare` 60s (the config-derived budget).
- **One split probe; disclosure fails safe** (sweep S3-7): the `/transfer/status` probe is a single shared hook (60s stale, retries on — a failure no longer sticks as "single host" until a remount). **Feature gates** (the transfer UI) enable only on `available === true`; **§12's disclosure on destructive dialogs** ("a copy may remain on the robot") leans the other way — only a confirmed single-host answer suppresses the note; unanswered or failing shows it (`useRobotCopyMayRemain`).
- **Pre-arm failures are not hidden** (sweep S2-7): 2+ consecutive prepare failures surface amber on the Ready card (Start still works via the synchronous full-start fallback), and retries back off exponentially from 30s to a 5-minute cap. The recorder does not file these probes as captures (→ capture_store §3.4).
- **Non-intrusive**: monitoring display comes from the monitor's raw / no-decode + best_effort path. Payload decoding is isolated in `topic_probe`.
- **Per-screen image-subscription budget**: previews subscribe only while their tab is visible and release on leave; sub cameras are forced to low resolution; aggregate cards (System etc.) use only the orchestrator's API values and never open a new subscription. At most one full-resolution stream at a time.
- No real paths in the frontend / no hardcoded pipelines / schemas and settings are handed over by the backend.
- Endpoints wait for `GET /api/v1/config` to complete before rendering (render gate). Hardcoded fallbacks are dev-only.
- Dangerous operations (double start, topic changes) are suppressed while recording. Destructive operations (Discard / Delete / Reset / End early) always have a confirm modal with Cancel.
- Time-series charts are unified on uPlot.
- Shared configuration: [config](config.md).
